title: API: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history
description: Implement the route body in app/api/routers/stocks.py (currently a 501 stub). Route signature and response_model are already wired.

checklist.step: Route signature + HistoryResponse schema already defined — confirm no shape changes needed
Implement handler: fetch via the cached data provider, map to HistoryResponse
Handle unknown ticker -> 404 per docs/architecture/API.md error cases
Write integration test (FastAPI TestClient, mocked data provider) covering 200, 404, 503
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Only fetch the interval actually requested: `provider.get_daily_ohlcv()` for `interval=daily`, `provider.get_weekly_ohlcv()` for `interval=weekly` — not both, unlike `/analysis` which always needs both for Screen 1/2. A `weekly`-interval request is therefore the only way this endpoint can raise `InsufficientHistoryError` (the shared `YFinanceProvider._MIN_WEEKLY_BARS = 26` floor baked into `get_weekly_ohlcv` itself, per the `DataProvider` protocol), mapped to `422` the same way `/analysis` does. Rejected: unconditionally calling both methods regardless of `interval` (matches `/analysis`'s pattern but wastes a fetch/cache-read the caller didn't ask for, and would force a daily-interval history request to fail on thin weekly history it never needed).
decisions.rationale: The `DataProvider` protocol has two separate single-interval methods with no way to ask for 'just daily, don't touch weekly' short of not calling the weekly method — so which method(s) to call per `interval` is a real branch point the docs don't spell out. Fetching only what's needed is the minimal-surprise reading of `interval` as a real filter, and keeps a `daily`-interval chart usable for a very recently listed ticker that a `weekly`-interval request to the same endpoint would legitimately reject.

decisions.decision: `range` accepts `<N>d` | `<N>w` | `<N>m` | `<N>y` (e.g. `1y`, `6m`, `90d`) or the literal `max`, validated via FastAPI's `Query(pattern=...)` (so a malformed value is a standard `422` HTTPValidationError, no custom code needed). The window is trimmed server-side after fetching the provider's full history (the `DataProvider` protocol takes no date-range argument — see `app/data/cache.py`'s module docstring), anchored on the most recent bar actually present in the fetched frame rather than on today's wall-clock date. Rejected: yfinance's own broader period vocabulary (`ytd`, `5d` with no unit letter, etc.) — API.md's only documented example is `1y`, and accepting yfinance-specific spellings the doc doesn't mention would leak an implementation detail into the public contract; also rejected anchoring the trim on `datetime.now()`, since the SQLite cache can be up to 24h stale (`_CACHE_TTL`) and a delisted/thinly-traded ticker's history may not reach the present at all — either case would silently return fewer bars than the requested range implies.
decisions.rationale: API.md documented the `range` query param's existence and one example value but not its accepted grammar or what a bad value should do, and the `DataProvider` protocol/cache explicitly punt date-range trimming to the caller (per their own docstrings) without saying where an anchor date should come from — both were real gaps this change had to close to have a testable contract.

decisions.decision: Declared the route's `422` response as an `anyOf` of `HTTPValidationError` (malformed `range`) and `ErrorDetail` (insufficient weekly history), mirroring the exact pattern already used by `POST /api/portfolio/positions` for its own dual-shape `422`, rather than inventing a new documentation convention.
decisions.rationale: Two structurally different failure modes both legitimately return `422` on this route (FastAPI's own query-validation error vs. this handler's `InsufficientHistoryError` mapping); reusing the existing `anyOf` precedent keeps the OpenAPI snapshot honest about both possible bodies instead of only documenting whichever one was declared last.

comments.summary: An unbounded numeric `range` value (e.g. `range=999999999y`, or an arbitrarily long digit string like `range=99999999999999999999999d`) matches `_RANGE_PATTERN` (`^(max|\d+[dwmy])$`, no digit-count bound) but crashes `_trim_to_range`'s `pd.DateOffset` arithmetic with an unhandled `ValueError`/`OverflowError`, which FastAPI turns into a generic `500` instead of the `422` the endpoint's own contract promises for a bad `range`. Verified directly with `TestClient`: `range=999999999y` returns `500`. Non-blocking (pathological input, not on any realistic client path) — filed as a follow-up rather than blocking.

The 404 (unknown ticker) integration test only exercises `interval=daily`; no test exercises `interval=weekly` hitting the identical `TickerNotFoundError` -> 404 mapping through `get_weekly_ohlcv`. Low risk (shared exception-handling code), non-blocking.
